text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's airforce is moving to purchase a second-hand VIP passenger aeroplane worth Z$300 million either from the German airforce or from a commercial airline in the same country in a bid to increase its fleet.

- Zimbabwean health workers who were dismissed by the government after going on strike to press for better salaries and working conditions appealed to president Robert Mugabe to intervene as they said they had exhausted all avenues for a negotiated settlement of their grievances.

- The Zimbabwe government is understood to be seeking a private developer for the long-stalled multi-billion dollar Batoka hydro-electricity project, which was initially a joint venture between Zimbabwe and Zambia before the latter withdrew from the project.

- Zimbabwean justice, legal and parliamentary affairs minister Emmerson Mnangagwa said on Thursday his government was committed to press freedom and would recommend that certain changes be made to laws that currently inhibit the operations of journalists.
- Several junior doctors and nurses dismissed by the Public Service Commission (PSC) for going on strike to press for better salaries and working conditions have begun reapplying for their jobs.

- President Robert Mugabe on Thursday launched a fund-raising campaign for the proposed new Catholic University with a call for the Catholics community to take the initiative to raise about Z$10 million for the first construction stage.
